items.title: Reading classic dynpro flow logic remotely over ADT (HTTP): is there an endpoint, or only RFC?
items.author: AlexandrePassarelli
items.text:
Hi all, 
 This morning I was answering a question about the partner tab in VA01 (function group V09C, screen 1000), and I wanted to read the flow logic of that screen to see which modules run inside LOOP WITH CONTROL. I read most standard code through ADT, and for classes, function modules and includes everything is there. For classic screens I got stuck. 
 What I checked, on S/4HANA 2023 (SAP_BASIS 758) and S/4HANA 2025 (816): 
 The ADT discovery document ( /sap/bc/adt/discovery ) has no collection for classic screens in either release. The only "screen" in it is the value help for logical database selection screens. 
 The where-used list does know the screen: a where-used on PBO module IS_ENHANCEMENT_01 returns screen 1000 as object type FUGR/PS , with a /sap/bc/adt/vit/wb/... URI. I haven't found a source endpoint behind it. 
 Over RFC there is a way: SVRS_GET_VERSION_DYNP_40 is RFC-enabled and has a D022S_TAB table parameter, which is the flow logic. IMPORT_DYNPRO is RFC-enabled too, but it returns only the header ( D020S ) and the fields ( D021S ). RPY_DYNPRO_READ has everything, but it is not RFC-enabled. 
 So my question: is there an ADT (HTTP) endpoint that returns the flow logic of a classic screen, read-only, that I'm missing? Or is the honest answer "SAP GUI or RFC"? 
 And if you work with ADT in VS Code or in Eclipse without SAP GUI, how do you look at PBO/PAI today? 
 In the V09C case I got around it from the other side: SAP's own IS-Oil enhancement implementation OIG_SAPLV09C_01 works on the current table control line, so that module has to run inside the loop. But I would like to see it, not deduce it.

items.title: #Demystifying AI Series — Ep 3:# "You Asked AI. It Answered. But Can You Stake Your Job on It?"
items.author: Benjelloun_Mhammed
items.text:
DEMYSTIFYING AI SERIES · EPISODE 03 

 "You Asked AI. It Answered. But Can You Stake Your Job on It?" 
 The episode topic owner @petepalme , 
 💡 AI gives you answers fast. But when you're working in a regulated environment — finance, HR, legal, procurement — fast isn't the same as right. Here's how SAP is trying to solve the trust problem. 
 The Question That Keeps Coming Up 
 Here's a scenario most SAP professionals recognize. 
 You're in a meeting. Someone pulls up a number from an AI assistant. It looks right. It sounds confident. The presentation moves on. 
 Three days later, someone finds the error. 
 Maybe it was a rounding issue. Maybe the AI pulled data from the wrong fiscal period. Maybe the logic was fine but the underlying data wasn't governed the way everyone assumed. 
 The number was wrong. And your name was on the slide. 
 AI operates at speed. Regulated environments operate at consequence. The question isn't "can AI help?" The question is: how do you know when to trust it? 
 The Problem With Confident-Sounding Wrong Answers 
 Here's what makes AI tricky in enterprise settings. 
 Traditional software fails loudly. A broken query returns an error. A misconfigured report produces blank cells. You know something went wrong. 
 AI fails quietly. It produces a coherent, well-formatted, confident-sounding answer — and that answer can be wrong. Not obviously wrong. Plausibly wrong. The kind of wrong that gets past the first check. 
 In a consumer app, that's annoying. 
 In procurement, that's a compliance breach. 
 In financial reporting, that's a SOX issue. 
 In HR, that's a potential legal exposure. 
 What the AI sees: a question and a dataset. 
 What you see: a decision that might get audited. 
 That gap is the trust problem. 
 What SAP Built to Close That Gap 
 SAP's answer has three parts — mapped to what they call "relevant, reliable, responsible AI." 
 Relevant — the AI works from your data, not a generic model of the world. SAP Business Data Cloud creates a governed data layer across your SAP landscape so Joule is grounded in the same data your financial close, procurement cycle, and HR processes run on. 
 Reliable — the data feeding the AI is trustworthy in the first place. Governance, data quality, defined ownership — these aren't AI features, they're data management fundamentals. But they're what make AI outputs auditable and defensible. 
 Responsible — the AI operates within the boundaries your organization has defined — access controls, compliance rules, audit trails. When Joule executes a workflow, there is a log. 
 These aren't just positioning words. They're architectural decisions SAP made because enterprise customers made it very clear: AI that can't be audited will not be adopted. 
 What It Still Cannot Solve 
 Here is where I want to be honest — because this is where AI enthusiasm often goes wrong. 
 Grounding and governance make AI safer. They don't make AI infallible. 
 The AI still reasons. And reasoning can go wrong in ways that are hard to catch without domain expertise. An AI with accurate, governed data can still draw the wrong conclusion. It can miss a business rule that isn't codified anywhere. It can apply general logic to a situation that has an exception your team has always handled manually. 
 The safeguard isn't better AI. It's you. 
 A well-grounded AI gives you a reliable starting point and a traceable output. What it can't give you is the judgment that comes from knowing your industry, your organization, your specific process — and the three things that went wrong last year that never made it into any system. 
 That knowledge lives in people. And it's exactly what turns an AI answer into a decision you can stake your name on. 
 A Different Way to Think About AI Trust 
 Forget "do I trust AI?" That's the wrong question. 
 You don't trust a spreadsheet — you verify it. You don't trust a report — you review it. The tool produces output. You apply judgment to that output. AI is no different. 
 High-stakes, regulated, first-time decisions: review carefully. Let the AI do the legwork but own the conclusion. 
 Routine, well-precedented, low-variance tasks: let the AI run. Spot-check. Move on. 
 The SAP professionals who navigate this well aren't the ones who blindly trust AI or reflexively distrust it. They're the ones who develop a calibrated instinct for which is which — and build that instinct through practice. 

 Your Turn 
 In your SAP environment — finance, HR, supply chain, or something else — what's the decision you'd be most reluctant to let AI make autonomously right now? 
 Drop it in the comments. That answer probably tells you more about your AI adoption frontier than any roadmap will. 
 ⏭ Next episode: SAP BTP's AI Foundation — the engine room that powers everything Joule does, and why it matters even if you never touch it directly.

items.title: #Demystifying AI Series — Ep 2 # Meet Joule, Why Calling It a "Chatbot" Completely Misses the point
items.author: Benjelloun_Mhammed
items.text:
Demystifying AI Series — Episode 2: 
 "Meet Joule — and Why Calling It a 'Chatbot' Completely Misses the Point" 
 You've heard of Joule. You probably filed it under "another AI assistant." Here's why that mental model is the most expensive misunderstanding you can make right now. 

 The Chatbot Trap 
 Let me tell you something about chatbots. 
 We've all used them. The little pop-up in the bottom-right corner that says "Hi! I'm here to help!" and then fails to answer a single useful question. 
 You type. It responds. You type again. It responds again. Nothing actually happens. 
 That experience has conditioned most of us to expect exactly nothing from anything called an "AI assistant." Which means when Joule shows up in your SAP system, there's a good chance you dismiss it before you even try it. 
 I get it. I felt the same way. 
 But here's the thing — Joule is not a chatbot. And the difference isn't marketing language. It's architecture. 
 So What Is It, Actually? 
 Joule is SAP's AI copilot. But that word — copilot — is doing a lot of work. 
 A chatbot sits outside your system and talks at you. 
 Joule lives inside your SAP landscape. It knows your data. It understands your processes. It has context about what you're doing, what your business does, and what the next logical step is — because it's connected to the same data that runs your company. 
 When you ask Joule something in S/4HANA, it doesn't just search the internet. It looks at your purchase orders, your inventory levels, your open approvals. It gives you an answer grounded in your actual business reality. 
 That's not a chatbot. That's something genuinely different. 
 And it works across the suite — S/4HANA, SuccessFactors, Ariba, SAP Build, and more. You don't switch tools. You just ask. 
 When Joule Stops Talking and Starts Doing 
 Here's where it gets really interesting. 
 Most people think of AI as something that answers. Joule also acts. 
 By end of 2025, SAP has 40 Joule Agents running across its portfolio, built on over 2,100 Joule Skills. Let me unpack that for a second. 
 A Joule Skill is a specific capability — a trained action. "Retrieve the status of purchase order X." "Draft a job description based on this role profile." "Summarize the key risks in this contract." These aren't responses. They're executions. 
 A Joule Agent goes further. It chains those skills together, makes decisions, and works through a task autonomously — with you in the loop at the right moments, not at every step. 
 Think about what that means in practice. 
 Instead of navigating five screens to check on an overdue invoice, you ask. Instead of pulling three reports to understand a procurement anomaly, Joule surfaces it. Instead of manually triggering an approval workflow, Joule handles the routing. 
 The work doesn't disappear. It just stops sitting on your plate by default. 
 The Part Nobody Explains: Why Joule Actually Knows Your Business 
 Here's the question most people don't ask: how does Joule know all of this about your company? 
 The answer is SAP Business Data Cloud. 
 Think of it as the memory layer. A unified, governed data foundation that connects SAP and non-SAP data — finance, HR, supply chain, procurement — into one coherent picture. When Joule answers a question or executes a task, it's drawing from that picture. 
 This is what SAP means when they say "relevant, reliable, responsible AI." 
 Relevant — because the answers come from your data, not some generic model of the world. 
 Reliable — because the data is governed, not a wild west of spreadsheets and exports. 
 Responsible — because access controls, compliance rules, and audit trails still apply. 
 A chatbot has whatever you typed into the chat window. Joule has your business. 
 What This Means for How You Work 
 Let me be direct about something. 
 If you're an SAP professional and you haven't seriously tried Joule yet — now is the time. Not because it's perfect. It's not. But because the professionals who understand its capabilities today will be the ones shaping how it's adopted tomorrow. 
 Here's what I've noticed: the people who get the most from Joule aren't the ones who use it as a search bar. They're the ones who push it. They ask it to execute, not just explain. They test its limits. They figure out where human judgment is still essential — and where it genuinely isn't. 
 That critical judgment — knowing when to trust the AI and when to override it — is a skill. And like any skill, it gets sharper with practice. 
 A Chatbot Answers. Joule Acts. That Distinction Will Define Your Next Few Years. 
 Calling Joule a chatbot is like calling S/4HANA "a spreadsheet." 
 Technically you can see the resemblance. Practically, you've completely missed the point. 
 Joule is not a feature you activate and forget. It's a new way of interacting with enterprise software — one that will become the default interface for SAP systems over the next few years. The professionals who figure that out early won't just work differently. They'll think differently about what their job actually is. 
 And that, I'd argue, is worth understanding. 

 Your Turn 
 Have you already seen Joule in your SAP system? What was your first reaction — excited, skeptical, or somewhere in between? Drop a comment — I'm genuinely curious whether the chatbot instinct kicked in, and whether something changed it. 
 ⏭ Next episode: You Asked AI. It Answered. But Can You Stake Your Job on It?" .

items.title: SAP Enterprise Service Management Q3 2026 Innovation Highlights
items.author: rmwilhelm
items.text:
As SAP's Autonomous Enterprise vision continues to take shape across our portfolio, in Q3 2026 we delivered powerful new capabilities for SAP Enterprise Service Management (SAP ESM) customers, partners, and practitioners. Whether you are modernizing HR service delivery, managing financial shared services, or looking to drive higher self-service adoption across the enterprise and every business function, the Q3 2026 release has something for you. 
 Before we dive in, we’re excited to share our customers’ value stories! Take a moment to register for our upcoming webinars and hear about our customers’ deployment journeys and value achieved from a unified, AI led, shared service operations with SAP ESM. 🚀 Tuesday, November 10, 2026 Cracking the Code on HR Service Delivery: Enercon's Journey Featuring Enercon and their journey in unifying HR shared service delivery moderated by HR Tech analyst, Anita Lettnik. Register here . 🚀 Thursday, November 19, 2026 Smarter, Faster, Unified: SAP’s Journey to AI-Powered Shared Services SAP’s global deployment with over 4000 service professionals live today, serving employees, partners and customers across XX business functions. Register here . 
 Now, let’s dive into the Q3 2026 innovation highlights including insights on autonomous assistants coming your way! For even more detailed insights on our Q3 2026 service innovations, register here for the Q3 2026 Release Overview on November 5th hosted by our product management team. 
 Intelligent case flow: Less effort with faster resolution 
 Case management in SAP ESM has proven to deliver the flexibility organizations need to model their shared service processes across the enterprise, coordinating complex workflows between automation and human action. The Q3 2026 enhancements to Case Flow reduce manual steps for both service representatives and administrators, allowing structured service processes to progress more naturally and more efficiently without unnecessary intervention. 
 Auto Complete Conditions for Input Steps in Case Flow 
 Input steps within a case flow allow service representatives to capture or update structured data in context without navigating away from the case. Until now, however, marking an input step as complete was always a manual action, even when the required conditions were clearly satisfied. 
 With this Q3 2026 release, administrators can now define conditions under which an input step will automatically mark itself as complete. When those conditions are met, for example, when specific field values have been set or when a case reaches a particular status, the system evaluates the configured logic and completes the step without requiring a service representative to take action. 
 Why it matters: 
 High-volume, structured processes benefit most. Think onboarding workflows, procurement inquiries, or HR case handling where multiple input steps follow predictable completion patterns. 
 Service representatives can focus on the steps that genuinely require their judgment, rather than clicking through steps the system can already identify as complete. 
 Administrators retain full control over when auto-completion applies, using the same familiar condition builder available throughout the Case Designer. 
 Auto Trigger for Case Approval Step 
 Approval steps in SAP ESM case flows are a critical governance mechanism, ensuring that key decisions are reviewed by the right people before a case proceeds. However, a common source of delay in approval-heavy workflows is simply that service representatives forget, or are too busy, to manually submit the approval request. 
 This enhancement allows administrators to configure an approval step to auto-submit as soon as its preconditions are met. Once the case reaches the configured state and all entry conditions are satisfied, the approval request is triggered automatically, without service representative intervention. 
 Why it matters: 
 Eliminates a common bottleneck in approval-gated workflows, particularly in financial shared services and compliance-driven processes where timely approvals are essential. 
 Works alongside existing precondition configuration, giving administrators precise control over when auto-submission is appropriate. 
 Approvers still receive requests and must act. This feature automates the submission, not the decision itself. 
 Accelerate Financial Service Delivery with Contract Accounts 
 For organizations delivering financial shared services, whether handling billing inquiries, payment disputes, collection workloads, or contract account management, having complete financial context within the service case is not a nice-to-have; it is essential. The Q3 2026 release introduces a deeply integrated Contract Account View, connecting SAP ESM directly to SAP Cloud ERP FI-CA financial data and bringing it into the agent's hands without the need to switch systems. 
 Contract Account View: Financial Documents, Invoices, Payments, and Collections 
 Service representatives working on financial inquiries can now see a complete picture of the customer's financial position right from the ESM agent desktop, without navigating to SAP Cloud ERP transaction screens. These include: 
 Financial Documents and Open Items: All FI-CA transactions for the past 365 days (configurable) are displayed, aggregated by document number. 
 Invoices: The last 12 months of invoices, billing documents, and billing plans are available, each with a direct link to the PDF printout. 
 Payments: All payment documents posted in the last 365 days are visible with real-time, color-coded status tags. 
 Collections: The full collections history from SAP Cloud ERP FI-CA is surfaced directly in ESM, covering dunning records, returns, and write-offs. 

 Contract Account View: Payment Arrangements, Locks, and Correspondence 
 Beyond raw financial data, the Contract Account View also provides service representatives with the context needed to understand active agreements, account restrictions, and prior correspondence, all without leaving the service agent desktop. 
 Payment Arrangements: All Promise to Pay agreements and Installment Plans for the contract account are visible in either card or table format. 
 Locks: Active and expired locks applied to the contract account are displayed, including lock type, reason, and date range. 
 Correspondences and Bank Data: Complete correspondence history, key attributes, and bank data, available in a dedicated tab. 
 This provides service representatives with a comprehensive financial picture in one place. 

 Elevating the self-service experience 
 The self-service application is how employees experience enterprise service management directly. Two Q3 2026 enhancements give administrators more precise control over what employees see and how they interact with their cases, resulting in a cleaner, more focused experience and fewer unnecessary support contacts. 

 Controlled Case Visibility in List View 
 In organizations where SAP ESM supports multiple lines of business, not every case type is intended for employee self-service visibility. With this Q3 2026 update, a new attribute has been added to the case type configuration to specify self-service relevance. Only cases belonging to case types that have been marked as self-service relevant in Case Type Configuration will appear in the employee's list. Cases associated with internal, service representative-only, or back-office case types will not be visible in the self-service interface. 
 Why it matters: 
 Employees see only the cases that are relevant and actionable for them, reducing confusion and erroneous selection. 
 Administrators gain precise control over the self-service experience, aligning what employees see with the organization's service delivery model. 
 This is particularly valuable for organizations running ESM across multiple functions such as HR, Finance, IT, and Procurement, where different case types serve very different audiences. 
 Enhanced Case Communication History 
 Understanding the full history of a case, including who said what, when, and through which channel, is fundamental to the self-service experience. Before this release, timeline events and case conversations were combined in a single Conversations tab, which made it harder to quickly locate a particular event or communication. 
 This enhancement restructures how case history is presented in the self-service interface, making it easier to locate specific events and communications, reducing inquiries back to the service representative and improving resolution times. 
 Why it matters: 
 A dedicated Timeline tab now presents all case events in chronological order, including status changes, assignments, workflow transitions, and other system-level activities, giving employees a clear audit trail of everything that has happened on their case. 
 The Conversations tab has been refined to focus on actual communications. A new Past Conversations section surfaces all non-internal notes, providing employees with a clear record of the dialogue between them and the service team. 
 Internal notes intended only for service representatives remain hidden from the employee-facing view, ensuring operational transparency is maintained without exposing confidential service team communications. 
 Preview: Autonomous Assistants 
 One of the most exciting themes at SAP SAPPHIRE and SAP Connect was the emergence of autonomous, AI-led assistants within SAP ESM. These are not incremental improvements to existing features; they represent a fundamentally different way of working, where Joule Work takes on complex, multi-step service and finance tasks with contextual intelligence and minimal human intervention. We are pleased to share an early look at two assistants currently progressing through Early Adopter Care, with general availability coming soon. 
 Recurring Receivables Assistant 
 Managing recurring revenue operations at scale is complex. Collections specialists, invoicing teams, subscription managers, and accounts receivable clerks each work within their own slice of a highly interconnected process, and when an exception occurs, resolving it typically requires manual coordination across multiple systems and stakeholders. 
 The Recurring Receivables Assistant coordinates execution across subscription orders and contracts, invoices, disputes, payments, and collections. The assistant helps teams prioritize collections, manage subscription contract changes, correct invoices, and resolve customer disputes and payments across multiple applications and solutions with clearer issue context and faster customer communication. 
 The assistant supports the core business stages across the receivables lifecycle: 
 Prioritize: Surfaces high-impact accounts, explains risk drivers, and recommends the next-best collection action, so collections specialists focus effort where it matters most. 
 Prevent: Detects invoice rejection risk before downstream impact occurs, identifies likely root causes, and recommends corrections, reducing exceptions before they slow collections. 
 Correct: Identifies contract data issues, validates corrections, simulates billing impact, and guides subscription specialists through the update, unblocking invoice and payment flow. 
 Resolve: Investigates payment exceptions and unmatched payments, connects invoice and contract context, and guides AR clerks through resolution, closing issues with less manual investigation.

items.author: marcel_schaefer
items.text:
The following blog post is relevant only for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Please note that Developer Extensibility is required. 

 Use Case: 
 At the time of writing this blog, the only available use case for BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD~CHANGE_INVOICE_TYPE is for country France. With this BAdI you can overwrite the value found in customizing activity "Determine Process Type and Invoice Attributes for Accounting Document Type". 

 Implementation: 
 To implement, use method "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud~change_invoice_type" in BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD (enhancement spot ES_EDOCUMENT_CLOUD). The method “change_invoice_type” receives the source data in the importing parameter “is_source_data”, "iv_source_key", "iv_source_type", "iv_edoc_type" and "iv_edoc_guid". The changing parameter “ CV_INV_TYPE ” allows you to change the invoice type determined by the customizing table. 
 Implementation Steps: 
 Create implementation for enhancement spot ES_DOCUMENT_CLOUD. 
 Create BAdI implementation for EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD. 
 (Optional) Create BAdI Filter for Country and/or Generic Filter. 
 Create implementing class for BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD, which implements the interfaces "if_badi_interfaces" and "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud". 
 Implement method "change_invoice_type" of interface "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud" in your BAdI class. 
 Activate your BAdI implementation.

items.title: SAP Sales & Service Cloud V2:Setting Up Principal Propagation with OAuth2SAMLBearer Authentication
items.author: Yogananda
items.text:
This is my 350th blog post, and I'm excited to continue sharing insights, experiences, and lessons learned with the community. 
 Introduction 
 When integrating SAP BTP services with SAP Sales Cloud Version 2 or SAP Service Cloud Version 2 or ESM , one of the most common requirements is ensuring that the identity of the logged-in user flows seamlessly from the source BTP application into the target SAP Cloud system. This is known as Principal Propagation . 
 Without principal propagation, every API call would authenticate as a technical/service user — losing all user context, audit trails, and authorization logic that depends on who is actually logged in. With it, the end user's identity is securely carried through, enabling fine-grained access control and meaningful audit logs on the SAP Sales/Service Cloud side. 
 This blog walks you through the complete setup using the OAuth2 SAML Bearer Assertion Flow — the recommended approach for BTP-to-SAP Sales & Service Cloud V2 connectivity. 

 How It Works — The Big Picture 
 User (logged into BTP app)
 │
 ▼
BTP Destination (OAuth2SAMLBearerAssertion)
 │ ── Generates a SAML assertion carrying the user's identity
 ▼
SAP Sales/Service Cloud V2 Token Service
 │ ── Validates the assertion against the trusted certificate
 ▼
Returns an OAuth2 Access Token (scoped to that user)
 │
 ▼
API Call executed as the propagated user The trust between BTP and SAP Sales/Service Cloud V2 is established by registering BTP's X.509 certificate as a trusted issuer inside the SAP Sales/Service Cloud V2 tenant. 
 Prerequisites 
 Access to your SAP BTP Cockpit (subaccount level) 
 Admin access to your SAP Sales Cloud V2 / Service Cloud V2 tenant 
 Ability to call REST APIs on the tenant (e.g., via Postman, Bruno, or curl) 
 Step 1: Download the BTP Trust Certificate 
 Log in to the SAP BTP Cockpit and navigate to your subaccount. 
 Go to Connectivity → Destinations → Download Trust (top-right area of the Destinations page). 
 A .pem certificate file will be downloaded. 
 Open the file and copy only the certificate content — the block between (but not including) the header and footer lines: 

 -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIEXzCCA0... ← copy everything between these lines
-----END CERTIFICATE----- 
 Keep this certificate value handy — you'll need it in the next step. 
 Step 2: Configure Inbound OAuth2 Trust in SAP Sales/Service Cloud V2 
 SAP Sales/Service Cloud V2 needs to know about BTP as a trusted SAML assertion issuer. This is done via a dedicated IAM Service REST API on your tenant. 
 Important restriction: Only one OAuth2 SAML Bearer Inbound Configuration can exist per tenant. 
 2a. Check if a Configuration Already Exists 
 Send a GET request to check the current state: 
 GET <Your-Tenant-Host-URL>/sap/c4c/api/v1/iam-service/oauth2InboundConfiguration 
 If a configuration exists with the same BTP certificate → you can reuse it as-is. 
 If a configuration exists with a different certificate → update it (Step 2b). 
 If no configuration exists → create a new one (Step 2c). 
 2b. Update an Existing Configuration (PUT) 
 PUT <Your-Tenant-Host-URL>/sap/c4c/api/v1/iam-service/oauth2InboundConfiguration/<id>
Content-Type: application/json

{
 "id": "<existing Id found in Step 2a>",
 "clientAppName": "<A meaningful name, e.g. BTP-SalesCloud-Trust>",
 "certificate": "<Certificate content from Step 1>"
} 
 2c. Create a New Configuration (POST) 
 POST <Your-Tenant-Host-URL>/sap/c4c/api/v1/iam-service/oauth2InboundConfiguration
Content-Type: application/json

{
 "id": "<BTP Subaccount UUID (This is to easily identify or you can provide your own UUID v4 format>",
 "clientAppName": "<A meaningful name, e.g. BTP-SalesCloud-Trust>",
 "certificate": "<Certificate content from Step 1>"
} 
 2d. Save the Response Values 
 A successful POST or PUT returns a JSON response like this: 
 {
 "value": {
 "id": "...",
 "grantType": "SAML2_BEARER",
 "nameIdType": "EMAIL",
 "spEntityId": "...",
 "audience": "<AUDIENCE>",
 "tokenServiceUrl": "<TOKEN_URL>",
 "clientId": "<CLIENT_ID>",
 "scopes": ["<SCOPE_ID>"],
 "clientAppName": "...",
 "certificate": "..."
 }
} 
 Note down these four values — you'll need them in Step 3: 
 Field Used As 
 audience Audience in BTP destination 
 tokenServiceUrl Token Service URL in BTP destination 
 clientId → appears as CLIENT_ID Client Key in BTP destination 
 scopes[0] → SCOPE_ID Scope in BTP destination 
 Step 3: Create the BTP Destination 
 Now configure a destination in your BTP subaccount that uses the inbound configuration values you just collected. 
 Go to SAP BTP Cockpit → Subaccount → Connectivity → Destinations → New Destination . 
 Fill in the following fields: 
 Property Value 
 Name Your choice (e.g., SalesCloudV2_PrincipalProp ) 
 Type HTTP 
 URL <Your SAP Sales/Service Cloud Tenant Host URL> 
 Authentication OAuth2SAMLBearerAssertion 
 Audience <AUDIENCE> from the inbound config response 
 AuthnContextClassRef urn:none 
 Client Key <CLIENT_ID> from the inbound config response 
 Token Service URL <TOKEN_URL> from the inbound config response 
 Scope <SCOPE_ID> from the inbound config response 
 nameIdFormat urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress 
 The nameIdFormat value tells the system to use the user's email address as the SAML NameID — this is how the user identity is matched on the SAP Sales/Service Cloud V2 or ESM side. 

 Step 4: Configure Trusted Domains in SAP BTP Authorization & Trust Management 
 As a final step, ensure that your SAP Sales/Service Cloud V2 tenant domain is registered as a trusted domain in SAP BTP's Authorization and Trust Management service (XSUAA/SAP Cloud Identity Services). 
 Refer to the official SAP documentation: Configure Trusted Domains for SAP Authorization and Trust Management Service . 
 This ensures that SAML assertions issued by BTP are only accepted by explicitly trusted target systems — an important security boundary. 

 Summary 
 Here's a quick recap of the end-to-end setup: 
 Step 1 → Download BTP X.509 Trust Certificate
Step 2 → Register certificate as Inbound OAuth2 Config on SAP Sales/Service Cloud V2
Step 3 → Create OAuth2SAMLBearerAssertion Destination in BTP using response values
Step 4 → Register SAP Sales/Service Cloud V2 domain as trusted in BTP Auth & Trust 
 Once complete, any BTP application or service using this destination will automatically propagate the logged-in user's identity to SAP Sales/Service Cloud V2 — without requiring users to re-authenticate or sharing technical credentials. 
 Key Takeaways 
 Principal Propagation bridges the identity gap between BTP and SAP Sales/Service Cloud V2, preserving the real user context across systems. 
 The trust is certificate-based — BTP's signing certificate is registered directly in the SAP Sales/Service Cloud V2 IAM service. 
 The fixed UUID ( 34f8b9d2-78c2-4617-bcf2-6eb36403c667 ) is a well-known system identifier for this configuration — don't change it. 
 Only one inbound configuration is allowed per tenant, so manage it carefully across teams. 
 User matching relies on email address as the SAML NameID — ensure users exist with the same email in both systems. 
 Share to your colleagues or Have questions or ran into issues during the setup? Drop them in the comments below.

items.title: Provisioning an SAP Cloud Identity Services Tenant via Self-Service Request in SAP for Me
items.author: AlexDong
items.text:
SAP Cloud Identity Services · How-To 
 Provisioning an SAP Cloud Identity Services Tenant via Self-Service Request in SAP for Me 
 A practical, step-by-step walkthrough of requesting your test or production tenant directly from SAP's central customer portal — no support ticket required. 🗓 ️ Updated October 2026 ⏱ ️ ~8 min read 👤 For SAP administrators & S-user holders 
 SAP Cloud Identity Services is the backbone for authentication, single sign-on, and identity provisioning across your SAP landscape. Before you can configure any of that, you need a tenant . This guide shows you how to request one yourself through SAP for Me — SAP's central customer portal for managing products, systems, and entitlements. Before you start: do you already have a tenant? A tenant may already have been created for you automatically as part of a bundle with an SAP cloud solution. Always check first — if a tenant exists and you are one of its administrators, go straight to the Administration Console instead of requesting a new one. New tenants are created only if there are no existing tenants bound to your Customer ID. 
 What's in this guide 
 Prerequisites 
 Two starting points in SAP for Me 
 Flow A — Get a tenant from Portfolio & Products (step-by-step) 
 Flow B — Get a tenant from Systems & Provisioning (bundled) 
 After provisioning & next steps 
 00. Prerequisites What you need Details 
 An S-user ID With your SAP for Me credentials and the appropriate authorizations to request/provision systems for your Customer ID. 
 Confirmed there's no existing tenant Check View Assigned Tenants and Administrators . A tenant is reused across SAP cloud solutions — you usually want one productive tenant for out-of-the-box SSO. 
 Know your region For EU Access contracts, pick a tenant located in Europe. Region choice affects performance and compliance. 
 A target resource group (Flow A) You'll select a Path to a resource group during the wizard. 
 01. Two starting points in SAP for Me 
 SAP for Me offers two different dashboards from which you can obtain a tenant. Pick the one that matches your scenario: Dashboard Use it when… 
 Portfolio & Products 
 The commercial catalog of what you purchased You want to explicitly request a test or production tenant for integration with SAP-managed cloud ERP applications, Joule, and other supported solutions. The tenant comes with SAP-managed integration configurations. → Flow A 
 Systems & Provisioning 
 Where you view, request, activate & manage cloud tenants You're provisioning an SAP cloud solution and want a tenant bundled with it, preconfigured and in the same region. The tenant is created automatically as part of that request. → Flow B 
 02. Flow A — Request a tenant from Portfolio & Products 
 This is the classic self-service "Get Tenant" path. Follow the steps below. 1. Log on to SAP for Me and open the Portfolio & Products dashboard 
 Sign in at me.sap.com with your S-user ID and password, then open the Portfolio & Products dashboard. SAP for Me landing page — the Portfolio & Products dashboard. 2. Go to the My Product Packages tab and select the SAP Cloud Identity Services tile 
 Open the My Product Packages tab, then click the SAP Cloud Identity Services tile to open its details. Selecting the SAP Cloud Identity Services tile under My Product Packages. 3. Open the Applications tab and choose Start Provisioning 
 Inside the product, switch to the Applications tab. On the SAP Cloud Identity Services tile, choose Start Provisioning . The Create Solution wizard launches. The Applications tab — choose "Start Provisioning" to launch the Create Solution wizard. 4. Fill in General Information 
 In the first step of the wizard, provide the following and then choose Next Step : 
 Entitlement System — read-only; displays the system ID of SAP Cloud Identity. 
 Name — a unique name for the solution. Max 63 characters, lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens and periods only; must start and end with a letter or number. 
 Path — use the Value Help to select a path to a resource group. 
 Business Type — choose Test or Production . You can't rename a solution after you create it. Decide on the name carefully before moving on. Step 1 — General Information. Entitlement System is pre-filled; you set Name, Path and Business Type. 5. Configure parameters — select a region 
 In the Configure Parameters step, select the region where the tenant will be hosted, then choose Review . Step 2 — Configure Parameters. Pick the hosting region for the tenant. 6. Review your entries and choose Finish 
 On the Review step, double-check everything — especially the Name and Business Type, which can't be changed later — then choose Finish . Your provisioning request starts immediately. Step 3 — Review and Finish. The request is submitted the moment you confirm. 7. Track status on the Resources tab until it's Ready 
 Provisioning takes a few moments. The solution resource reaches Ready status only when all tenants are successfully provisioned and the integrations are fully established. Monitor progress on the Resources tab. You can find out the tenant address within the detail page. The Resources tab — watch each resource move from In Progress to Ready.   Done! Once the tenant is provisioned, you can proceed to provision your SAP cloud applications — the new SAP Cloud Identity tenant will be available for selection during that process. 
 03. Flow B — Get a tenant from Systems & Provisioning (bundled) 
 Use this flow when you want a tenant bundled with an SAP cloud solution e.g. SAP Cloud ALM . There's no separate "request tenant" button here — when you provision your application and no SAP Cloud Identity Services tenant is available, one is created automatically when you submit the request. 
 Step 1 — Open Systems & Provisioning → Provisioning tab 
 Log on to SAP for Me, open the Systems & Provisioning dashboard, and go to the Provisioning tab. 
 Step 2 — Choose Start Provisioning for your solution 
 Under Systems to be Provisioned , choose Start Provisioning for the SAP cloud solution you want to bundle with SAP Cloud Identity Services. If the button is disabled… automatic tenant creation isn't available for this case. You must first request a tenant manually in the SAP BTP cockpit , then return to SAP for Me and restart provisioning so the new tenant appears for selection. 
 Step 3 — Complete the Start New Provisioning Request dialog 
 Provide the following, then choose Submit : Field What to enter 
 Region The data-center location for the solution tenant. Not available for all applications; may be system-determined by your contract. 
 Integration with SAP Cloud Identity Services Select a test or production SAP Cloud Identity tenant. For some apps you can integrate a test application tenant with a productive identity tenant. 
 Owner of SAP Cloud Identity Services Own systems (same Customer ID) or Shared systems (a tenant from a different Customer ID shared with your company). Start New Provisioning Request Start New Provisioning Request Region Europe (Frankfurt) ▼ Integration with SAP Cloud Identity Services Production Test ▼ Owner of SAP Cloud Identity Services Own systems Shared systems ▼ Cancel Submit The Start New Provisioning Request dialog — a tenant is auto-created on Submit if none exists. 
 04. After provisioning & next steps 
 Activate your tenant. Depending on the path, you may receive an account activation email. Open it, follow the link, set your administrator password, and continue into the Administration Console. 
 A self-service tenant is not preconfigured. You must configure it for your specific authentication and provisioning scenario (identity sources, SSO, provisioning targets, etc.). 
 Reuse before you request. For out-of-the-box SSO between SAP cloud solutions, use a single productive tenant wherever possible. 
 Special cases: multi-region businesses can request additional per-region tenants; each SAP SuccessFactors instance should get its own tenant via the SuccessFactors Upgrade Center. Products delivered on SAP BTP? Products running on a customer-managed SAP BTP subaccount usually don't trigger automatic tenant creation — you request the tenant in the SAP BTP cockpit instead. On an SAP-managed subaccount, the tenant is provisioned automatically with the application. Written as a how-to guide for SAP administrators. UI mockups are illustrative — replace the dashed slots with real screenshots from your environment before publishing. Source: SAP Help Portal — Get Your Tenant (SAP Cloud Identity Services) . Always confirm against the latest official documentation.

items.title: Joule Work：实现对话、业务洞察与 Agent 协同的一体化工作空间
items.author: Helen_Han
items.text:
即将推出的 Joule Work ，把对话交互、业务数据查询、任务进度追踪、异常分析以及 Agent 协同能力整合至动态工作空间内。用户只需用自然语言描述业务目标，系统就会结合业务上下文自动调度所需信息与功能，支撑后续的分析与处理。完成一项工作，无需在多个应用之间来回切换。 
 从 Conversations 中提出问题，到 Spaces 中集中分析，再到通过 Joule Studio 扩展 AI 能力，Joule Work 将这些体验连接起来，让业务目标与后续行动紧密衔接。 
 注：Joule Work 暂未正式发布（ GA ），最终发布范围与上线时间请以 SAP 后续官方公告为准。 

 图示：Joule Work 将对话、业务工作空间以及开发体验整合在统一界面当中。 
 产品介绍：Joule Work 

 通过自然语言开启工作：Conversations 
 Conversations 是和 Joule 交互对话的入口。用户可以描述想要查询的信息或是希望完成的任务，在对话过程中补充筛选条件、持续追问，从而获取对应的指引与结果。对于多步骤的复杂任务，对话也可以作为进入 Spaces 的起点。 
 举个例子：业务人员想要了解某项任务的进展，可以先抛出问题，再基于返回的结果做进一步分析。这种交互方式让用户直接从业务问题入手，不用事先确定需要打开哪一款应用。 

 图示：在 Conversations 中查询退货率异常原因、查看仓库各项指标，并将分析结果转入 Space 。 

 围绕单一任务集中开展工作：Spaces 
 Spaces 是围绕特定业务目标搭建的动态工作空间，它会把相关的数据、工具和业务上下文汇聚在同一个环境里，并且根据当前任务动态调整展示内容。适合那些需要持续分析、多项对比或者分多步推进的工作场景，全程保留业务关注点与上下文信息。 
 以财务关账为例，财务负责人可以从“ 本月关账遇到了哪些阻碍 ” 这个问题开始，在同一个工作空间查看相关数据、待办事项、异常信息以及 Agent 的活动记录，判断哪些事项需要优先处理，再结合已启用的能力推进后续工作。 

 图示：Spaces 在工作空间内汇总各个国家、仓库的退货率图表，同时你还可以在右侧继续对话、补充分析。 

 基于业务需求进行扩展开发：Develop / Joule Studio 
 如果企业团队需要构建专属 AI 能力，可以从 Joule Work 的左侧导航栏进入 Joule Studio。业务人员和开发人员可在 Joule Studio 中搭建适配自身业务流程的 Agents、应用以及自动化流程。 

 Joule Work、Assistant 和 Agent 的协作关系 
 Joule Work 是用户输入目标、查看信息、推进各项工作的交互界面；Joule Assistants 结合业务角色与流程上下文进行任务统筹；Joule Agents 负责执行专项任务，调用对应的数据、工具以及应用完成工作。 
 简单来说：用户在 Joule Work 中提出业务目标，由 Assistant 统筹调度所需能力，再由 Agents 执行具体任务，用户查看结果并按需做出决策。企业原有业务系统依旧承担核心业务处理工作。 
 企业现有的数据权限、业务授权以及审核机制保持不变。Joule Work 只是对接这些能力的交互界面，底层管控能力依托 SAP Business AI Platform ；自动化程度需要结合具体业务场景进行配置。

items.title: Initiative does not appear on PB screen despite being assigned in related items page
items.author: tejas_kamble23
items.text:
Hello Experts, 
 We are facing an issue in SAP PPM/PS integration and would like to understand whether anyone has encountered similar behavior. 
 Scenario 
 When an initiative is assigned to or removed from an item through the Related Items page: 
 The initiative assignment/removal is performed successfully. 
 The initiative description is correctly displayed in the Item Overview tab. 
 However, the corresponding Initiative ID and Initiative Description in Project Builder are not refreshed automatically. 
 Observed Behavior 
 The values in Project Builder are updated only after making an additional manual change to the item (for example, modifying the item description, adding a character, and saving again). 
 Expected Behavior 
 Project Builder should reflect the latest Initiative ID and Description immediately after the initiative is assigned or removed from the Related Items page, without requiring any additional save action. 
 SAP Response 
 We raised an OSS Incident and received the following clarification from SAP: 
 SAP confirmed that DFM synchronization supports either: 
 Initiative ↔ Item synchronization, or 
 Item ↔ PS Project synchronization. 
 The combined synchronization path Initiative ↔ Item ↔ PS Project is not supported in SAP standard . 
 SAP referred to KBA 3515319 – "Synchronization isn't working between Item/PPM-Project/PS-Project" . 
 SAP stated that synchronization from Initiative directly through Item to PS Project and vice versa is not delivered in standard SAP code . 
 According to SAP, the observed behavior is working as designed and is therefore not considered a bug . 
 SAP suggested submitting an enhancement request through the Customer Influence / Customer Connection process if this functionality is required in standard product behavior. 
 Questions 
 Has anyone implemented a custom solution to automatically synchronize Initiative data from Item to Project Builder? 
 Is there any BAdI, enhancement spot, event, or workflow exit that can be leveraged to trigger the synchronization? 
 Is there any standard report, synchronization program, buffer refresh mechanism, or background job that can update Project Builder immediately after Related Item changes? 
 Has anyone found an SAP Note or recommended workaround other than manually re-saving the item? 
 Any guidance, implementation experience, or best practices would be greatly appreciated. 
 Thank you

class_idea.title: Finding and reusing existing SAP enhancements in classic screens: VA01 partner tab case study
class_idea.why_now: Three related items today: a user-exit question for the VA01/VA02 partner tab (ref 33), a blog on reusing an existing SAP enhancement in the same function group (ref 111), and a question on reading dynpro flow logic over ADT (ref 100).
outline: Why modifying form routines such as LV09CF63 is fragile
Locating enhancement options: BAdI definitions, enhancement spots, implicit enhancements, customer exits
Checking what SAP or industry solutions already enhanced in the same function group (V09C) and reusing it
Reading dynpro flow logic: SE80/SE51 versus ADT; what ADT does not expose
Clean core classification: classic extension (level B/C) versus released extension points
Upgrade and regression risks, and how to document the choice
class_idea.exercise: In a sandbox system, open function group V09C and screen 1000 (partner tab). List every enhancement option that touches the partner table control (search the PBO modules, where-used on the form routines, and check enhancement implementations). Make the Partner field display-only for one partner function using the least invasive option you find. Test it in VA01 and VA02 at header and item level, then write a short note on upgrade risk.

deep_dives.title: Changing screen field properties in VA01/VA02 without editing LV09CF63
deep_dives.explanation:
Ref 33 asks for a user exit or BAdI alternative to the form routine LV09CF63 for setting input/display properties of partner fields on the VA01/VA02 Partner tab, at header and item level. Editing a standard include or relying on a form-level modification is fragile: it is a modification, it needs adjustment at upgrade, and it is invisible to most enhancement searches.

Ref 111 is titled as a tip for exactly this case. Its one-line summary says you can lock the VA01 partner fields without changing LV09CF63 by reusing an existing SAP enhancement in the same function group. Only the headline is available to me, so I cannot confirm the details. Ref 100 supports the idea: it mentions the enhancement OIG_SAPLV09C_01, an IS-Oil implementation that runs on the current table control line in function group V09C. That is an existing hook where the current line is available.

A practical method: open function group V09C and screen 1000, then find the PBO modules that loop over the partner table control. Check for explicit enhancement points and enhancement implementations already active in the system. Look at what data the existing enhancement has in scope (the current table control line) and whether field attributes can be changed there. Verify all of this in your own release, as available hooks differ between systems and industry solutions.

Be careful about the trade-offs. Reusing an industry-solution enhancement may depend on a business function being active, and it may not be present in every customer system. Document the dependency, and test header and item level separately in both VA01 and VA02.

deep_dives.title: Item category versus schedule line category after a plant change (ref 71)
deep_dives.explanation:
The poster in ref 71 derives the item category VBAP-PSTYV from a custom table when VBAP-WERKS changes. The logic sits in USEREXIT_MOVE_F8ELD_TO_VBAP. A manual plant change works. An ABC/ATP plant switch does not: the availability check runs only for the original item category, and the old schedule line data in MVERF is later used to overwrite the newly determined schedule line category from RV_SCHEDULING_TYPE_DETERMINE.

The underlying issue is ordering. The schedule line category depends on the item category, and the ATP check consumes schedule line data. If PSTYV is changed after the check has run, the cached results are stale. A late user exit therefore cannot fully fix it.

The sensible direction, which the post's analysis points to, is to set the item category earlier than the availability check, or to force a re-determination of the schedule lines after the change. This is a suggestion, not a verified fix. Trace with a watchpoint on VBAP-PSTYV and on the MVERF entries to see where they are written and consumed in the ABC flow.

The thread has no answer. Treat any fix as release-specific: check for standard BAdIs or events before the availability check, and confirm the behavior on your S/4HANA release, since changing standard structures such as MVERF directly would be a modification.

deep_dives.title: Remote access to classic dynpro flow logic: ADT versus RFC (ref 100)
deep_dives.explanation:
Ref 100 is a well-documented gap report. On S/4HANA 2023 (SAP_BASIS 758) and 2025 (816), the ADT discovery document at /sap/bc/adt/discovery has no collection for classic screens. A where-used on a PBO module returns screen 1000 of function group V09C as FUGR/PS with a /sap/bc/adt/vit/wb/... URI, but the author found no source endpoint behind it.

Over RFC the author lists three function modules. SVRS_GET_VERSION_DYNP_40 is RFC-enabled and returns flow logic in D022S_TAB. IMPORT_DYNPRO returns only the header (D020S) and fields (D021S). RPY_DYNPRO_READ returns everything but is not RFC-enabled.

The diagnostic order is reusable. First check the discovery document for a matching collection. Then use where-used to obtain object URIs and see whether they resolve. Finally compare function modules by RFC-enabled flag and by which table parameters they fill. Check the RFC flag yourself in SE37, since I only have the author's statement.

No answer is given, so as a team default, use SE80 or SE51 for flow logic and treat the RFC route via SVRS_GET_VERSION_DYNP_40 as a read-only workaround. The author notes it is a version-management function, so validate that it returns the active version.

digest.headline: Quiet day for core ABAP: classic screen enhancement questions, eDocument BAdIs for Cloud Public Edition, and several AI/MCP posts with little technical detail.

interview_questions.question: Users want partner fields on the VA01/VA02 Partner tab to be display-only. Currently the team edits form routine LV09CF63. How do you approach this?
interview_questions.answer: Editing LV09CF63 is a modification, so it needs adjustment at every upgrade and is hard to find. I would first look for supported hooks. I would check the V09C screen 1000 PBO modules and see which enhancement points, BAdIs or existing enhancement implementations are available. Ref 100 mentions OIG_SAPLV09C_01, which runs on the current table control line and could be a candidate. I would verify in the actual release that it is active and that the needed business function exists. I would test header and item level in both VA01 and VA02. Finally I would document the dependency and the fallback if no supported hook exists.

interview_questions.question: A custom user exit changes the item category after a plant change, but the schedule line category stays based on the old item category. How do you analyze it?
interview_questions.answer: I would first establish the order of events. The schedule line category depends on the item category, and the ATP check uses schedule line data. If PSTYV changes after the check has run, the stored data is stale. In ref 71 the author found that MVERF data from the original category overwrites the newly determined schedule line category from RV_SCHEDULING_TYPE_DETERMINE. I would set watchpoints on VBAP-PSTYV and the MVERF entries to see where they are written and read in the ABC flow. Then I would look for a standard enhancement that runs earlier than the availability check, or one that forces a re-determination. I would avoid patching MVERF directly. I would confirm all this in the target release because the thread has no verified answer.

interview_questions.question: When do you override eDocument type or invoice type with the EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD BAdI in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition rather than use configuration?
interview_questions.answer: Configuration first. The standard determination uses customizing such as 'Assign eDocument Type to Accounting Document Type/Billing Document Type/Delivery Type'. Ref 85 advises searching SAP Notes and checking whether source-application customizing can separate the cases before writing code. The BAdI is a last resort: IF_EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD~CHANGE_EDOCUMENT_TYPE changes CV_EDOC_TYPE from IS_SOURCE_DATA, IV_SOURCE_KEY and IV_SOURCE_TYPE. Methods like CHANGE_INVOICE_TYPE (ref 107) are currently limited to France according to the post, and GET_VARIABLE_KEY (ref 83) changes the key used for customizing lookup. A wrong value can silently select the wrong number range or document type, which has compliance impact. Use Developer Extensibility, filter by country, and test in the tenant.

digest.overview:
Today's material is thin on core ABAP depth. The most useful items are developer questions: reading classic dynpro flow logic over ADT or RFC (ref 100), changing the VA01/VA02 partner tab without editing LV09CF63 (refs 33, 111), and a plant-change problem where the schedule line category stays on the old item category (ref 71). A series of three short posts covers EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD BAdI methods for S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (refs 83, 85, 107).

The rest is AI and BTP content: an AI supplier recommendation series (refs 105, 124, 128), MCP posts (refs 117, 121), and China availability announcements for the ABAP environment and Kyma (refs 24, 23). Several items are only excerpts or teasers (refs 87, 110, 7), so their claims cannot be checked. Treat these as pointers, not sources.

Editing form routine LV09CF63 is a modification.
It costs you at every upgrade.

- what the existing ones can see (e.g. the current table control line)

Verify in your own release that the hook is active.

post_drafts.title: Stale schedule lines
post_drafts.text:
*Changed the item category in a user exit and the schedule line category did not follow?*

A poster reports exactly this after an ABC/ATP plant switch.
ATP ran on the old item category.
Old MVERF data then overwrote the new schedule line category.

Takeaway: ordering matters.
Set the item category *before* the availability check, not after.

No accepted answer yet, so test on your release.

Source: https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-q-a/schedule-line-category-not-redetermining-after-custom-code-changes-item/qaq-p/14506913
